record.result: I added `TaskStore.delete(task_id)` in `src/tasklib/store.py`, and the visible tests pass (127 passed). It validates the ID with `validate_id`, so `ValueError` is raised for non-positive IDs, non-integers and bools. It then removes the task from the store's dict and returns that same `Task` object. A valid ID that isn't in the store raises `KeyError`, including on a second deletion, and an error leaves the store unchanged. I didn't touch the next-ID counter or the persistence code. Deleting therefore never reuses an ID, even after deleting every task, and JSON save/load keeps the remaining order and the counter. I didn't add tests for these cases, since test files are off limits, so the save/load behaviour after a deletion is untested.
